one_line: Eighth-century Jain scholar-monk of Jalor, observing schools and merchant networks across western Indian trade routes under Pratihara suzerainty.

appearance.age_look: mid-40s, slender but healthy build, slightly stooped from study
appearance.face: oval face, wheatish Rajasthan complexion, sharp thoughtful eyes, straight nose, neatly trimmed short beard and moustache; default expression is calm, observant and gently curious with a slight scholarly intensity.
appearance.hair: dark brown-black hair, closely cropped and tidy, with a simple white cotton head-cloth (pagri-like wrap) tied low and flat around the crown, ends tucked in at the back, leaving forehead and ears visible.
appearance.costume: He wears a modest 8th-century Jain monk’s ensemble adapted to western India: a plain off‑white cotton upper cloth (uttariya) draped over both shoulders and wrapped around the torso, covering chest and upper arms, with a slightly longer tail folded over his left forearm; a soft, ankle‑length unstitched lower garment (dhoti-style) in the same off‑white cotton, pleated in front and wrapped securely at the waist; under this a simple long-sleeved light beige tunic is just barely visible at the neck and wrists for added modesty; his feet are in simple brown leather sandals suitable for long walks between towns and upashrayas; no metal jewellery, only a small wooden bead wristband on his right hand signifying restraint, and a finely stitched cloth satchel at his left hip for manuscripts.
appearance.signature: A rectangular palm-leaf manuscript bundle of the Kuvalayamala, wrapped in a light tan cloth with two dark red tie-cords, held in his left hand, along with a slender wooden stylus tucked alongside the bundle.

ref_desc: Uddyotana Suri is a mid-40s Jain monk with an oval wheatish face, short beard, cropped dark hair under a flat white head-cloth, in off-white draped cotton robes and brown sandals, carrying a tan-wrapped palm-leaf Kuvalayamala manuscript with dark red ties and wooden stylus.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character of Uddyotana Suri: a mid-40s, slender Jain scholar-monk from 8th-century Jalor with an oval wheatish face, sharp thoughtful eyes, straight nose, and neatly trimmed short beard and moustache. His dark brown-black hair is closely cropped, topped by a simple flat white cotton head-cloth wrapped around the crown. He wears plain off-white cotton draped robes: an upper cloth covering both shoulders and torso, and an ankle-length dhoti-style lower garment, with a light beige long-sleeved tunic subtly visible at neck and wrists for modest layering. Show his simple brown leather sandals and a small wooden bead wristband on his right wrist, plus a cloth satchel at his left hip. In his left hand he holds a rectangular palm-leaf Kuvalayamala manuscript bundle wrapped in tan cloth, bound with two dark red cords, with a slender wooden stylus tucked alongside. Use off-white, light beige, brown, dark red, and tan as the dominant colours, and present him front-facing in a neutral pose, clearly showing face, hair, robes, sandals, and manuscript bundle for consistent redrawing in many panels.
